parole.significato: Used to form the dative case
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـه (-a,-e), from Proto-Turkic *-ka (“dative case”).

parole.significato: Derives gerunds and adverbial participles. Adverbs derived this way are generally used in rhyming reduplications.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـه (-a,-e), from Proto-Turkic *-ü (“gerundive suffix”).

parole.significato: Used to form the optative mood of verbs
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـه (-a,-e), from Proto-Turkic *-gey (“optative-predictive future case”).
From Ottoman Turkish ـاق, from Proto-Turkic *-gak.

parole.significato: In Turkish, the plural is brought to the verb or stem of the verb in order to pull the plural in the imperative mood.
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *-elim.

parole.significato: Creates participles and relative clauses where
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـان (-an), from Old Anatolian Turkish [Term?], from Proto-Turkic *-gan.

parole.significato: Derives intransitive verbs from names of colors.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـر (-r, -er, -ar), from Proto-Turkic *-gar.
From Proto-Turkic *-čak.

parole.significato: like, -like, -ly; -ish; as if, as though; in the way of
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـجه (-ce), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *-če (orientative–prolative suffix).

parole.significato: Suffix appended to words to create a noun, denoting a profession, occupation or inclination.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـجی, from Proto-Turkic *-či.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـجك, from Proto-Turkic *-čük.

parole.significato: forms animal names, especially the names of birds and insects
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *-čin.

parole.significato: Used to form locative of nouns.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـده (-da, “locative suffix”), from Proto-Turkic *-te (“locative suffix”). Cognate with Karakhanid دا (-dā, “locative suffix”), Old Turkic 𐱃𐰀 (t¹a /⁠-ta⁠/, “locative suffix”).

parole.significato: A noun-forming suffix frequently denoting a "fellow of", "having in common", "sharing".
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـداش, from Proto-Turkic *-daĺ. Contraction of locative suffix -da/-de and eş “companion”.

parole.significato: used to form locative of nouns
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـده (-de, “locative suffix”), from Proto-Turkic *-te (“locative suffix”), front vowel variant of *-ta. Cognate with Karakhanid ـدا (-dē, “locative suffix”), Old Turkic 𐱅𐰀 (t²a /⁠-te⁠/, “locative suffix”).

parole.significato: Used to form ablative of nouns.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـدن (-den), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـدن (-den), from Proto-Turkic *-den.
From Proto-Turkic *-ti (past tense suffix).

parole.significato: forms realis verbal nouns, or non-subject participles.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـدك, from Proto-Turkic *-tuk.
From Ottoman Turkish ـدر (-dir), from Proto-Turkic *tur- (“to stand”). Cognate with Turkish durmak (“to stand, to stop”).
From Proto-Turkic *-tur (causative suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـك (-ek), from Proto-Turkic *-gek.

parole.significato: Derives adjectives from nouns and verbs.
parole.testo: A variation of -il (“derives deverbals and denominals”), from Proto-Turkic *-il or *-gil. Both variants likely merged with homophonic -il (“derives adjectives for onomatopoeia and colors”). See şırıltı (“onomatopoeia for flowing water”), kızıl (“red”) and yeşil (“green”). For words using the same su

parole.significato: Derives reflexive verbs from nouns and adjectives.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـال (-al, -el) or ـل (-l), a combination of Proto-Turkic *-(g)a (verb-forming suffix) and *-il (passive suffix).
From Proto-Turkic *-galï.

parole.significato: simple present and aorist tense marker
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـر (-r, -er), from Proto-Turkic *-ür. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰼 (r² /⁠-(e)r⁠/). Negative -mez are from Proto-Turkic *-meŕ, from Proto-Turkic *-me + *-er or *-ür (Azerbaijani -ər (“indefinite future suffix”) — -məz, but -ir (“simple present suffix”) — -mir).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـر (-er), from Proto-Turkic [Term?].

parole.significato: Derives nouns of habit or inclination from verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *-gan, *-gen.

parole.significato: Derives names of tools from verbs or nouns.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـكچ (-gaç, -geç) and sometimes ـكج (-gac, -gec), from Proto-Turkic *-gač, *-geč. In many cases in Modern Turkish the "g" falls off and the suffix presents as -aç/-eç.
From Ottoman Turkish ـگی (-gi), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـکو (-gü), from Proto-Turkic *-gü.
From Ottoman Turkish ـغن (-gın), ـغین (-gın), ـقین (-ḳın), ـكین (-gin, -kin), ـغون (-gun) or كون (-gun, -gün, -kun, -kün), from Proto-Turkic *-gïn, *-gun. Cognate with Kazakh -гін (-gin).
From Ottoman Turkish ـی (-i), from Proto-Turkic *-ni (“accusative suffix”).

parole.significato: Third-person singular possessive suffix denoting singular possession.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـی (-i), from Proto-Turkic *-si (“third-person singular possessive suffix”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـی (-i), from Proto-Turkic *-ig.

parole.significato: Suffix creating adjectives and/or (sometimes occupational) nouns directly from transitive verbs: -ive, -ous, -er
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـیجی (-ici), from Proto-Turkic *-gučï. By surface analysis, -i (deverbal nominal) + -ci (“-er”).

parole.significato: Derives participle forms of verbs; adjectival and/or resulting state or product of the action.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـیق (-ik) as well as Ottoman Turkish وق (-uk), from Proto-Turkic *-uk, synonymous to Proto-Turkic *-ïg.
From Proto-Turkic *-l. Cognate with Kazakh -іл (-il).

parole.significato: First-person singular possessive suffix denoting singular possession in words ending in a consonant.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish م (-m, ım, -im, “first-person singular possessive suffix”), from Old Anatolian Turkish م (-m, um, -üm, “first-person singular possessive suffix”), from Proto-Turkic *-im. Cognate to Old Turkic 𐰢 (m /⁠-m, -ım, -im, -um, -üm⁠/, “first-person singular possessive suffix”).

parole.significato: Conjugation of the verb "to be" for first-person singular, simple present tense.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـم, ـن (-im, -ım, -in, -ın, -en, “first-person singular suffix”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (-ven, “first-person singular suffix”), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *-bẹn (see ben (“I”)). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰢𐰤 (mn² /⁠-men⁠/, “first person singular suffix”), Kar

parole.significato: Derives nouns from verbs of an instance of, or a result of performing, the action implied by the verb.
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *-im.
From Proto-Turkic *-niŋ.

parole.significato: Second-person singular possessive suffix denoting singular possession.
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *-iŋ.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـنجی, from Proto-Turkic *-inč.

parole.significato: Forms converbs to talk about other actions done by the same subject.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـوب ultimately from Proto-Turkic *-ip. Cognate with Azerbaijani -ib.
Ottoman Turkish ـور (-ur, -ür), from Proto-Turkic *-gür.

parole.significato: Suffix creating present continuous tense, denoting action happening at the time.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـییور (-iyor, -ıyor), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـهیورر (-eyorur, -ayorur), ـهیور (-eyor, -ayor), from Old Anatolian Turkish یورمق (yorımaq), یورمك (yörimek), from Proto-Turkic *yorï- (“to walk”), which was used as an auxillary verb, compare Kazakh жүру (jürüw) where i
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـش (-iş), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـش (iş), from Proto-Turkic *-iĺ.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـش (-iş), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـش (-iş), from Proto-Turkic *-iĺč.

parole.significato: A suffix forming terms of endearment.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *-č.

parole.significato: Assimilated form of -gan after the vowels E / İ / Ö / Ü.
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *-gan, *-gen.

parole.significato: Used to form an adjectival or nominal meaning "that which belongs to."
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـكی (-ki), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـكی (ki), ـكم (kim). Inherited from Proto-Turkic *-ki
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish [Term?], from Proto-Turkic *-kir.

parole.significato: Passive suffix. Used to form verbs that affected by event(s).
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *-l-.
From Ottoman Turkish ـله (-la, -le), from Proto-Turkic *-la.

parole.significato: Noun-forming suffix frequently denoting a "wild and predatory animal".
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *-lan.

parole.significato: Suffix appended to nouns to derive verbs with various meanings.
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *-le (“suffix forming denominal verbs”). Possibly related to Proto-Mongolic *-le and Proto-Tungusic *-le.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـلك (-lik), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـلك (-lik), from Proto-Turkic *-lïk, from *-lik.

parole.significato: negates meaning of the verb. not, don't
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـمه, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *-me.

parole.significato: forms irrealis verbal nouns, or non-subject participles.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـمه, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *-me.
From Ottoman Turkish ـمك (-mek), from Proto-Turkic *-mek.

parole.significato: forms the necessitative mood must, shall, should, have to
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـملى (ـمالى (-malı), ـمهلى (-meli)), from Proto-Turkic *-melig.

parole.significato: Forms agent nouns from verbs, denoting professions. -er, -ant
parole.testo: Originally from Ottoman Turkish ـمن (-men), inherited from Proto-Turkic *-man, as in değirmen. In some Ottoman coinages it conflated with Persian ـمان (-mân, “-like”). Sense 1 is found mainly in language reforms' coinages, and was likely influenced by German -mann and English -man.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـمز (-mez, -maz), from Proto-Turkic *-meŕ.

parole.significato: Suffix creating subject past participles or impersonal perfective participles from verbs.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـمش (-miş), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـمش (-miş), from Proto-Turkic *-miĺ.

parole.significato: Used to form locative of nouns that already carry other case markers ending with vowels.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـندا (-nda, “locative suffix”), from Proto-Turkic *-nta (“locative suffix”), formed with *-n- (“oblique case marker”). Cognate with Karakhanid نْدا (-ndā, “locative suffix”), Old Turkic 𐰦𐰀 (n͡ta /⁠-nta⁠/, “locative suffix”).

parole.significato: Derives verbs of wish, desire, inclination towards the noun it is derived from.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ـسا (-sa), ـس (-se), evolved from the verb Proto-Turkic *sā- or *sā(j)- (“to count, to consider, to desire something, to count something among one's wishes”). Compare saymak. Cognates with Azerbaijani -sa, -sə, Karakhanid ـسا, ـسه.

parole.significato: Suffix of verb "to be" for subject "you" (informal).
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـسڭ (-sin), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (-sen, -sin, -san, -sın), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *sen. Cognate with Azerbaijani -sən. Compare -im (“first-person singular suffix”) from Proto-Common Turkic *ben (see ben (“I”)).
From Proto-Turkic *-zün (“third-person singular imperative suffix”). Cognate with Azerbaijani -sin, Uzbek -sin.
From Ottoman Turkish ی (-ï, “possessive marker”), from Proto-Turkic *-ï (“possessive marker”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰃 (i /⁠-ï⁠/).
From Ottoman Turkish ی (-ï, “adverbial suffix”), from Proto-Turkic *-u. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰆 (w /⁠-u⁠/).
From Proto-Turkic *apa (“mother, elder sister, aunt”).
From Ottoman Turkish ابلا (abla, “elder sister”), most likely from earlier *appa, from Proto-Turkic *apa (“mother, elder sister, aunt”). Compare ebe (“aunt, midwife”).
From Proto-Turkic *abuč-ka.
From Proto-Turkic *ăčaj.

From Ottoman Turkish آجی (acı, “bitter”), from Old Anatolian Turkish آجُو (acu, “bitter”), from earlier *āçıɣ, from Proto-Turkic *āčï-g (“bitter”), derived from Proto-Turkic *āčï- (“to become bitter”) (see acı-).

From Ottoman Turkish آجی (acı, “pain, ache”), from Old Anatolian Turkish آجُو (acu, “pain”), from Proto-Turkic *āčï-g. Unclear relationship to Etymology 1, see more at acımak (“to pity, to hurt, become sour”).

parole.significato: to hunger; be hungry, feel hunger, feel peckish
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آجیقمق (acıkmak, “to be hungry, to hunger”), from Old Anatolian Turkish آچقمق (açuqmaq, açıqmaq), from Proto-Turkic *āčïk- (“to hunger”), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *āč-. /t͡ʃ/ to /d͡ʒ/ after the succeeding vowel due to original long vowel in the first syllable, co

parole.significato: to pity, feel pity and compassion for
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آجیمق (acımak), from Proto-Turkic *ačï- (“to pity, have compassion”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آجیمق (acımak), from Proto-Turkic *āčï- (“to become bitter, sour”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آد (ad, “name”), from Old Anatolian Turkish آد (ad, ād, “name”), from Proto-Turkic *āt (“name”). Compare Azerbaijani ad, Gagauz aad, Turkmen at.

parole.significato: That which has been promised to be made an offering or that which has been made an offering as a sign of gratitude or f…
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *atā- (“to give name, to make a promise, to affiance, to beckon”) combined with the suffix -ak.

parole.significato: To intend or to vow to make an offering or an oblation to a power that is believed to be sacred for the purpose of maki…
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *atā- (“to give name, to make a promise, to affiance, to beckon”), which was derived from Proto-Turkic *āt (“name”) combined with the suffix Proto-Turkic *-(g)A. Doublet of atamak.
From ad- (“noun”) + -ıl (noun deriving suffix). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *āt (“name”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آدیم (adım, “step”), from Proto-Turkic *ātïm (“step”), a derivation from *āt- (“to walk”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آقمق, from Proto-Turkic *ak-. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ak-), Azerbaijani axmaq, Crimean Tatar aqmaq, Uzbek oqmoq, Uyghur ئاقماق (aqmaq), Khorezmian Turkic اقماق, Kumyk акъмакъ (aqmaq), Turkmen akymak, Bashkir ағыу (ağıw), Kazakh ағу (ağuw), Kyrgyz агуу

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آغساق (aġsak, “that droops on one side, lopsided, that limps in walking”), from Proto-Turkic *agsak (“lame”), derived from Proto-Turkic *agsa- (“to hobble, limp”). By surface analysis, aksamak + -k.

parole.significato: To limp, to hobble. (to walk lamely, as if favouring one leg)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آغسامق (aġsamak, “to droop and limp when walking”), from Proto-Turkic *agsa- (“to hobble”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آقسرمق (aksırmak, “to sneeze”), from Proto-Turkic *askïr-. Cognate with Azerbaijani asqırmaq, Gagauz ansırmaa, Salar axsırğusı, Turkmen asgyrmak.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آقتارمق, from Proto-Turkic *āgtar-. Cognate with Salar axdarğusı, Turkmen āgdarmak.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آقچه (akçe, (earlier) akça, “silver money, coin, a third part of a para, anciently a real coin of much greater value and a day's pay for a soldier, now a mere money of account”), from Proto-Turkic *ākča (“silver coin; money”), from Proto-Turkic *āk. By surface analysis

From Ottoman Turkish آقین (aqïn, “rushing tumultuously like a torrent, a foray, raid”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (aqïn, “raid”), from Proto-Turkic *akïn (“flow, stream”), from Proto-Turkic *ak- (“to flow”). See akmak (“to flow”). Cognate with Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽲𐽶𐽺 (akïn, “fluid, liquid”
From Ottoman Turkish آل (al), from Proto-Turkic *āl (“red, crimson”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰞 (āl) and akin to Proto-Tungusic *pula (“red”) and Proto-Mongolic *hulaxan (“red”)
From Proto-Turkic *āl (“trick, deceit; to deceive”).
From almak, from Proto-Turkic *al- (“to take”). Cognate with dialectal Kazakh алажақ (alajaq).
From Ottoman Turkish آلازلمق (alazlamak), related to al (“red”). Ultimately derived from Proto-Turkic *āl (“red, scarlet”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلدانمق (aldanmak), reflexive of آلدامق (aldamak, “to deceive, cheat, trick”), from Proto-Turkic *ālda-, a derivation from Proto-Turkic *āl (“device, trick”)

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلداتمق (aldatmak), causative of آلدامق (aldamak), from Proto-Turkic *ālda- (“to trick, fool”), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *āl (“device, trick, deceit; to deceive”). Cognate with Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐾁𐾀𐽰𐽹𐽰𐽷 (ʾʾltʾmʾk /⁠altamaḳ⁠/), Azerbaijani aldatmaq etc.

From Ottoman Turkish آلو (alev), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (alav), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *yal- (“to burn, blaze; flame”). Doublet of yalın. Cognate with Azerbaijani alov, Uzbek olov, Kazakh алау (alaw).
From Proto-Turkic *Alk- (“to finish; destroy; (refl.) perish, be exhausted, come to an end”).

From Ottoman Turkish آلقیش (alkış), inherited from Proto-Turkic *alkïš (“congratulation, benediction”), from Proto-Turkic *alka- (“to praise, to revere”). Cognate with Yakut алгыс (algïs, “praise; blessing”), Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐾁𐽲𐽶𐽿 (ʾʾlqyš /⁠alḳïş⁠/, “benediction, congratulation”). For the verb, see Old
From Ottoman Turkish آلمق, from Proto-Turkic *al- (“to take”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلپ (alp), from Proto-Turkic *alp (“difficult, hard; warrior”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلت (alt), from Proto-Turkic *al (“bottom, underside”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلتمش, from Old Anatolian Turkish التمِشۡ (altmış), from Proto-Turkic *altmïĺ. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰡𐰢𐱁 (l͡tmš /⁠altmïš⁠/, “sixty”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلتی (altı, “six”), from Old Anatolian Turkish آلۡتِی (altı, “six”), from Proto-Turkic *altï (“six”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰞𐱃𐰃 (l¹t¹i /⁠altï⁠/, “six”), etc.

parole.significato: gold, a yellow, elemental metal of great value, with atomic number 79
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلتون (altın, altun, “gold”), from Proto-Turkic *altun (“gold”). parole.significato: Not having much distance from the ground, not high; low.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish آلچاق (alçaḳ, “low, short in stature, shallow, vile, despicable”), from Proto-Turkic *ăl (“lower side, below, being below, lower”). According to Talât Tekin Turkish aşağı (from aşak) and alçak are doublets, since ĺč turns into ş in Common Turkic. But longs vowels do not fit toge
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آلن (alın), from Proto-Turkic *ālïn (“forehead”). Old Uyghur ʾʾlyn (alïn, “forehead”), Karakhanid اَلِنْ (alïn, “forehead”).
From the verb Proto-Turkic *alïn- (“to take on, to take for self”), derived from Proto-Turkic *al- (“to take, to hold, to defeat”) with the suffix Proto-Turkic *-ïn morphologically al- + -ın + -tı.
From Ottoman Turkish آماج (amaç), from Old Anatolian Turkish آماج (amaç), اوماج (omaç), from Proto-Turkic *um-. Cognate with Karakhanid اَمَجْ (amač), Azerbaijani amac, Southern Altai амаду (amadu).

From Ottoman Turkish عموجه (ʼamuca), from older آبجه (abıca, abuca), equivalent to Proto-Turkic *apa (“father”) + *-ča. Compare also Proto-Turkic *abučka (“uncle”). Nişanyan explains the change from /b/ to /m/ as an influence of Arabic عَمّ (ʕamm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آننه, انا, from Proto-Turkic *ana (“mother”), *eńe (“mother”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰣𐰀 (ana).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آنغت (angıt), آنغیت (angıt), آنغد (angıd) or آنغید (angıd), from Proto-Turkic *āŋkït (“wild duck”), shares common origin with Mongolian ангир (angir). Cognates with Azerbaijani anqut, Chagatai انقوت (anḳut), انقور (anḳur), Karakhanid اَنْكِتْ (aŋıt, anɣıt), Kumyk гьанк

parole.significato: To understand, to comprehend, to get.

parole.significato: to make mention of, to commemorate
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آڭمق (añmak), from Proto-Turkic *āŋ- (“to remember”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آننه, انا, from Proto-Turkic *ana (“mother”), *eńe (“mother”). Cognate with Chuvash анне (anne) and Old Turkic 𐰣𐰀 (ana).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آند (and), from Proto-Turkic *ānt (“oath”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰦 (n͡t), Azerbaijani and, and Southern Altai андык- (andïk-, “to prove”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آڭرمق (añırmak), possibly from Proto-Turkic *ïŋïra- (“to neigh; to bellow, purr”). Cognate with Azerbaijani anqırmaq.
From an (“mind, consciousness”) + -ıt, from Proto-Turkic *āŋ (“intelligence, ability to understand”).
From Ottoman Turkish آكیز (añız, “stubble”), from Proto-Turkic *aŋïŕ (“stubble field”).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *-p-.
From Proto-Turkic *apa (“mother, elder sister, aunt”). Compare ebe (“aunt, midwife”).

parole.significato: to be surprised, gape, not to know what to do
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اپوشمق (apuşmak, “to spread the legs, choke, run out of breath, to gape”). Akin to apış (“crotch”) and apul apul (“spreading the legs (adv.)”), derived from Proto-Turkic *āg (“crotch, the space between the thighs”). From Ottoman Turkish ایلمك (ilmek), from Proto-Turkic *īl- (“to hang on (smth.), hook”).

From Ottoman Turkish ایری (iri), from Proto-Turkic *idrig, see Azerbaijani iri for more.

parole.significato: pus (fluid found in regions of infection)

From Ottoman Turkish ایرمیك (irmik, “semolina”), from Proto-Turkic *yār- (“to split”).

From Ottoman Turkish قاڭرمق (kañırmak, “to pull aside, bend”), from Proto-Turkic *kaŋïr- (“to bend”).

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قراموق (karamuk), from Proto-Turkic *karamuk (“tares; corncockle”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قراواش (karavaş), from Old Anatolian Turkish قَرَوَاشْ (qaravaş), from Proto-Turkic *kara baĺč. Morphologically kara + baş. Compare Azerbaijani qarabaş.

parole.significato: crow, any bird, usually black, of the genus Corvus, having a strong conical beak, with projecting bristles

parole.significato: pike, javelin, dart, a long spear with a pointed tip made of iron used as a weapon
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قارغی (kargı, “pike, javelin”), from Proto-Turkic *kargu (“long reed”). Cognate with Azerbaijani qarğı and Turkmen gargy.

parole.significato: to condemn, to curse, to maledict

parole.significato: Consisting of things of different qualities; mixed, diverse, assorted.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قارشق (karışık, “mixed, adulterated, confused, disordered”), from قارشمق (karışmak, “to join and mix, to become confused and disordered, to interfere, to exercise control”), from Proto-Turkic *karïĺ- (“to be mixed with one another, to be tacked onto each other”), from

parole.significato: to stretch, to tighten, to contract, to strain, to flex

parole.significato: hoop, a circular band of metal, wood, or similar material used for forming part of a framework
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاصناق (kasnak, “tambour, embroidery hoop”), ultimately from a development of Proto-Turkic *kas- (“to tighten”).

parole.significato: groin, the crease or depression of the human body at the junction of the trunk and the thighs
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاصق (kasık, “groin”), from Proto-Turkic *kāsïk (“groin”). Cognate with Azerbaijani qasıq, Tatar касык (qasıq) and Turkmen gasyk.

parole.significato: Temporary stitching to tighten or to gather a part of a garment; tacking or basting stitches.

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاتق (ḳatıḳ, “anything added, anything eaten with bread to give a relish, a condiment”), from Proto-Turkic *katïk (“anything added”) from *kat- (“to mix, to add, to tie to”), equivalent to kat- + -ık. A cognate with Kazakh қатық (qatıq).

parole.significato: tinder, punk, touchwood, amadou, any spongy and flammable substance used to light fire
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاو (kav, “tinder, touchwood”), from Proto-Turkic *kiab (“tree fungus; dry grass”).

parole.significato: poplar, any of various deciduous trees of the genus Populus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قواق (kavak), from Proto-Turkic *kabak (“white poplar, willow”).
From Ottoman Turkish قاورامق (kavramak), from Proto-Turkic *k(i)arba- (“to grope, grasp”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاون (kavun), from Proto-Turkic *kagun.

parole.significato: kind of traditional dish prepared by mixing ground and roasted grain flour with sugar, butter, or honey
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاوت (kavut), from Proto-Turkic *kağut (“roasted wheat”), a root related to *kagur- (“to parch, roast”). Cognate with Azerbaijani qovut.

parole.significato: to meet, to reach, to achieve
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قاوشمق (kavuşmak), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (qavušmaq), from *qabuš-, from Proto-Turkic *kab-. Cognate with Kazakh қауысу (qawısuw), Azerbaijani qovuşmaq, etc.

parole.significato: to boil, to come to the state of vaporizing

parole.significato: to skip, play hooky, slack, loaf, evade
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قایتارمق (kaytarmak, “to recall”), from Old Anatolian Turkish قایترمق (qaytarmaq), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *kādït-, itself from Proto-Turkic *kād-.
From Ottoman Turkish قایق (kayık), from Proto-Turkic *kiayguk (“boat, oar”). Cognate with Azerbaijani qayıq, Crimean Tatar qayıq, Uzbek qayiq.

From Ottoman Turkish قاین (kayın), from Proto-Turkic *kadïŋ (“birch tree”). Compare Old Turkic [script needed] (kadıŋ), Uzbek qayin (“birch tree”), Kyrgyz кайың (kayıŋ), Kazakh қайың (qayıŋ), Yakut хатыҥ (xatïŋ) etc.
From Ottoman Turkish قاین (kayn, kayın, “wife's brother”), from Proto-Turkic *kādïn (“relative-in-law”). Unrelated to kadın, hatun.

parole.significato: to walk back from a previous decision or promise
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قایتمق (kaytmak, kayıtmak), from Proto-Turkic *kādït-, a derivation from Proto-Turkic *kād-.

From Ottoman Turkish گز (gez) ultimately from Proto-Turkic [Term?]. Cognate with Kazakh кез (kez) and Turkmen gezek.

parole.significato: To smell, to give out a scent.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قول (qol, “arm, sleeve, branch”), from Proto-Turkic *kol (“upper arm”). Cognate to Old Uyghur qwl (qol, “arm”), Karakhanid قُولْ (qōl, “arm”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قولتق (koltuk, “armpit; armchair”), from a development of Proto-Turkic *kol (“upper arm”).

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قولچاق (kolçak, “gauntlet; mitten”), from Proto-Turkic *kolčak (“muff, gauntlet”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قومق (komak), from Old Anatolian Turkish قومق (qomaq, “to put”), from Proto-Turkic *ko- (“to put”).

parole.significato: neighbour (a person living on adjacent or nearby land)

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوناق (konak), from Proto-Turkic *konak (“guest; lodging”); cognate with Azerbaijani qonaq, Bashkir ҡунаҡ (qunaq), Kazakh қонақ (qonaq), Kyrgyz конок (konok), Southern Altai конок (konok), Tatar кунак (qunaq) and Uzbek qoʻnoq. Doublet of konuk.

parole.significato: guest, visitor, a person who receives hospitality at the invitation of someone else

parole.significato: part of a footwear that covers the leg

parole.significato: nail (spike-shaped metal fastener used for joining wood or similar materials)

From Ottoman Turkish چیك (çiy), from Proto-Turkic *čï̄g (“wet, moist; dew”). Compare Old Turkic [script needed] (či, “wetness, moisture”). Cognate to Salar çıxsu, Turkmen çȳg (“wet, moist”); unrelated to Turkmen çīg (“raw”).
From Ottoman Turkish چیچك (çiçek), from Proto-Turkic *čeček. See Bashkir сәскә (säskä) for further cognates.
From Ottoman Turkish چیك (çiğ), from Proto-Turkic *čīg (“wet, moist; dew; raw”).

parole.significato: crocus, a flowering plant in the genus Crocus, from which saffron is obtained
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چیكدام (çiğdâm, çiğdem), from Proto-Turkic *čigdem (“crocus”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چكین (çeğin, çiğin, “ridge of the shoulder”), from Proto-Turkic *čekn (“part of shoulder between the neck and shoulderblade”), a word that Clauson links to Proto-Oghuz *čig- (“to knot”). Cognate with Azerbaijani çiyin, Khalaj çîin and Turkmen çigin.
From Ottoman Turkish چیكنهمك from Proto-Turkic *čayna- (“to chew”).

From Ottoman Turkish چوجق (çocuk, “pigling; child”), from Proto-Turkic *čōč- (“child; young pig”); from which also *čōčka (“pig”). Cognate with Azerbaijani çocuq (“child”) (archaic), Uzbek jujuq (“small child”), Turkmen jōjuk (“piglet”), Old Turkic 𐰲𐰆𐰲𐰹 (čočuk, “piglet?”).
From Ottoman Turkish چوق (çok), from Proto-Turkic *čok.
From Ottoman Turkish چولاق (çolak), from Proto-Turkic *čol- (“crippled; to deteriorate, dwindle; defect; short-statured”). Cognate with Kyrgyz чолок (colok), Kazakh шолақ (šolaq), etc.

parole.significato: cudgel, bat, truncheon, a stout stick with a rounded head used as a weapon
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوماق (çomak, “cudgel, bat, truncheon”), itself from Proto-Turkic *čomak (“mace, club”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چبوق (çibuk, çıbuk, çubuk), from Proto-Turkic *čöpik (“stick, twig”).

parole.significato: hole, pit, hollow, cavity, depression, sump, a place located at a lower level than its surroundings
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوقور (çukur, “hole, pit, hollow”), from Proto-Turkic *čukur (“hole, cavity, depression”), a derivation from *čok- (“to delve, dig”). Cognates Cognate of Azerbaijani çuxur, Chagatai چوقور (çuqur), Uyghur چوڭقۇر (chongqur) and Uzbek chuqur.

parole.significato: woodcock, any of several wading birds in the genus Scolopax, specifically Scolopax rusticola
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوللق (çulluk, “woodcock”), from Proto-Turkic *čulïk (“kind of bird”). Compare Old Turkic [script needed] (çulık).
From Proto-Turkic *čug.
From Ottoman Turkish چوكلمك (çökülmek), from Ottoman Turkish چوكمك (çökmek), from Proto-Turkic *čök-, morphologically çök- + -el- + -ti.

From Ottoman Turkish چوكمك (çökmek), from Proto-Turkic *čök-. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (čök-, “to kneel, sit down”), Azerbaijani çökmək, Southern Altai чӧгӧр (čögör), Kazakh шөгу (šögüw), etc.

From Ottoman Turkish چوكندی (çökündü, “fallen materials, sediment, deposit”), from Ottoman Turkish چوكونمك (çökünmek, “to kneel or crouch down, for sediment to settle”), from Ottoman Turkish چوكمك (çökmek, “to collapse, to fall down, for sediment to settle or be precipitated”), from Proto-Turkic *čö
From Ottoman Turkish چول, from Proto-Turkic *čöl (“steppe, desert”). Northern Luri چوول (çul, “steppe”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوكلمك (çöñelmek), ultimately derived from Proto-Turkic *čök-, whence çökmek.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوملك (çömlek, “an earthenware pot, especially a pipkin used in cooking”), derived from Proto-Turkic *čöŋgek (“a kettle, pitcher”), further origin is unknown. Cognates with Azerbaijani çölmə, Chuvash чӳлмек (čülmek), Crimean Tatar çülmek, Kazakh шөлмек (šölmek), Kyrgyz
From Proto-Turkic *čöŋ-.

parole.significato: A small thin branch of a bush or tree; a small straw-thin stick.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چوپ (çöp), from Proto-Turkic *čöp.

From Ottoman Turkish چوزمك (çözmek, “to untie, unfasten, loosen, unravel, solve”), from Proto-Turkic *čöŕ-. Cognate with Karakhanid [script needed] (çöžmēk, “to pull, stretch”), Azerbaijani çözmək (“to resolve”), Chagatai [script needed] (çözmek, “to take off, pull off, disperse”), Khorezmian Turkic

From Ottoman Turkish چوروك (çürük, “rotten, spoilt”), from Ottoman Turkish چورومك (çürümek, “to rot, to decay”), from Proto-Turkic *čüri- (“to sour, to spoil”), morphologically çürü- + -k. Cognate with Kazakh шірік (širik), Turkmen çüýrük.
From Ottoman Turkish چبان, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *čïbïkan (“jujube”), metaphorically extended to mean 'furuncle, rash'; then further evolved into the modern senses of 'boil, abscess'.

parole.significato: to leave, exit, quit, get out
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چیقمق, from Proto-Turkic *čïk- (“to go out”). Cognates Cognate with Azerbaijani çıxmaq, Gagauz çıkmaa, Salar çıq, Turkmen çykmak, Uzbek chiqmoq, Kumyk чыкъмакъ (çıqmaq), Kazakh шығу (šığuw), Nogai шыгув (şıguv), Kyrgyz чыгуу (cıguu), Southern Altai чыгар (čïgar), Tatar чыгу (çığ

parole.significato: spinning wheel, a domestic device for spinning yarn or thread from fibres using one spindle
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چقرق (çıkrık, “spinning wheel; capstan; jenny”), from Proto-Turkic *čığrık or *čıkrık (“something which revolves”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čakrám (“wheel”).

parole.significato: A small cloth bundle; a bindle.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چیقین (çıḳın, “a square cloth or handkerchief made into a round bundle”), from Proto-Turkic *čïgïn (“parcel, pack”), from *čïg- (“to tie up a parcel, to sew with small stitches”) + *-ïn.

parole.significato: act or way of going out of, getting out of, or leaving (a place), exit, egress; act or way of coming out or emerging, e…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چیقش (çıkış), from Proto-Turkic *čïk-ïĺ. By surface analysis, çık- + -ış. Cognate with Karakhanid جِقِشْ (čïqïš, “going out, way out, profit”), Kazakh шығыс (šığıs, “exit, east”), Kyrgyz чыгыш (cıgış, “exit”), Uzbek chiqish (“exit, emergence”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چنغراق (çıngırak, “bell”), itself from Proto-Turkic *čïŋra-. Compare to Southern Altai шаҥыра- (šaŋïra-, “to bell”), etc.
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *čïŋla-. Cognate with Salar çıñna.

parole.significato: To quickly shake a carpet, a rug etc.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چرپمق (çırpmak), derived from çarpmak (“to hit, to strike, to bump”), from Proto-Turkic *čap- or Proto-Turkic *čalp- (“to hit, to steal, to plunder”).

parole.significato: To struggle or to flutter with pain.
parole.testo: Derived from çarpmak (“to hit, to strike, to bump”), from Proto-Turkic *čap- or Proto-Turkic *čalp- (“to hit, to steal, to plunder”), morphologically çırp- + -ın- + -mak.
From Ottoman Turkish چیان (çıyan), from Proto-Turkic *čadan, possibly from Middle Chinese 蠆 (trhaejᴴ). Cognate with Bashkir саян (sayan).

parole.significato: snow-path, ice-path, a track or trail made in the snow or ice with the feet or using a shovel
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چیغیر (çığır, “snow-path”), from Proto-Turkic *čïgïr (“foot path, narrow track”). Cognate with Azerbaijani cığır and Tatar çığır.
From Proto-Turkic *ȫt.
From Proto-Turkic *öd (“time”).

parole.significato: to pay (give money in exchange for goods or services)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اودهمك (ödemek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫte-. Perhaps related with Proto-Tungusic *xuda- and Proto-Mongolic *kudaldu-. Cognate with Turkmen ȫdemek, Azerbaijani ödəmək, Bashkir үтәү (ütäw), Southern Altai ӧдӱ- (ödü-), etc. Compare also Dongxiang ghudandu, Manchu ᡠᡩᠠᠮᠪᡳ (uda

From Ottoman Turkish اودلك (ödlök, ödelek, “timid, cowardly”), possibly derived from Proto-Turkic *ȫt (“gall, bile”), with similar semantic relation to Humorism in Ancient Greece, only the gall bladder is associated with fear and courage, rather than anger. Compare Ottoman Turkish اودك (ödek, “cowar
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوفكه (öfke, “anger”), from Proto-Turkic *öpke (“lung, anger”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (öpkä), Kazakh өкпе (ökpe), etc.
From Ottoman Turkish اوكسورمك (öksürmek), from Proto-Turkic *üskür-. Cognate with Azerbaijani öskürmək, Chuvash ӳсӗр (üs̬ĕr), etc.

From Ottoman Turkish اوكسز (öksüz, “orphan”), from Proto-Turkic *ȫgsüz (“1. orphan, motherless child 2. mindless, dumb”). Originally a compound equivalent to ök (breast, chest, mother by metonymy) + -süz (“without, -less”) but ök has become obsolete in isolation. Cognate with Kumyk оьксюз (öksüz).

parole.significato: heel, the part of a shoe's sole which supports the foot's heel
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكچه (ökçe), from Proto-Turkic *ökče (“heel”); cognate with Azerbaijani ökcə, Bashkir үксә (üksä), Kazakh өкше (ökše), Kyrgyz өкчө (ökcö) and Turkmen ökje.
From Ottoman Turkish اوكوز (öküz, “ox”), from Proto-Turkic *öküŕ (“ox”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰈𐰛𐰈𐰕 (öküz, “ox”), Chuvash вӑкӑр (văk̬ăr, “bull”), Hungarian ökör (“ox”) a Turkic borrowing.

parole.significato: to kill, to murder (with accusative case)
parole.testo: By surface analysis, ölmek (“to die”) + -dir (causative). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *öltür- (“to kill”)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اولمك (ölmek, “to die”), from Old Anatolian Turkish اولمك (ölmek), from Proto-Turkic *öl- (“to die”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰇𐰠 (öl-, “to die”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اولچك (ölçek), from Proto-Turkic *ölč- (“to measure”).

parole.significato: to measure, to ascertain the quantity or size of a unit of material
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اولچمك (ölçmek), from Proto-Turkic *ölč- (“to measure”); cognate with Azerbaijani ölçmək, Bashkir үлсәү (ülsäw), Chuvash виҫ (viś), Kazakh өлшеу (ölšew), Kyrgyz өлчөө (ölcöö) and Uzbek oʻlchamoq
From Ottoman Turkish اولو (ölü, “dead”), from Proto-Turkic *ölüg (“dead”), derived from *öl- (“to die”). See öl- (“to die”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰇𐰠𐰏 (ölüg, “dead”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اولم (ölüm), from Old Anatolian Turkish اولوم (ölüm), from Proto-Turkic *öl- (“to die”). By surface analysis, öl- (“to die”) + -üm (“deverbal nominal”). Cognate with Khakas ӧлім (ölìm), Kyrgyz өлүм (ölüm), Southern Altai ӧлӱм (ölüm), Yakut өлүү (ölüü), Kazakh өлім (öli
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اول (öl), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *ȫl (“wet”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوك (öñ), from Proto-Turkic *öŋ, *oŋ.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوڭجه (öñce), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *öŋ (“front”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوپمك (öpmek), Old Anatolian Turkish اوپمك (öpmek), from Proto-Turkic *öp-. Compare Old Turkic 𐰇𐰯 (öp-).
From Ottoman Turkish اوردك (ördek, “duck”), from Proto-Turkic *ȫrdek (“duck”). Cognate with Karakhanid اۥرْدَكْ (ördek, “duck”).
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish اورلمك (örlemek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫrle-, a derivation from Proto-Turkic *ȫr- (“to rise”).

parole.significato: to knit; to darn; to braid, plait
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اورمك (örmek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫr- (“to plait”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ör-, “to plait, build”), Azerbaijani hörmək (“to plait”), Bashkir үреү (ürew, “to plait”), Khakas ӱрерге (ürerge, “to plait”), Kyrgyz өрүү (örüü, “to braid”), Turkmen örmek (“t
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اورسلمك (ürselemek, örselemek), from Old Anatolian Turkish اورسلمك (örselemek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫrsele-, ultimately a derivation from Proto-Turkic *ȫr- (“to rise”)

parole.significato: to cover with a clothing; to veil, to clothe
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اورتمك (örtmek, “to cover, wrap, veil, shut”) from Old Anatolian Turkish اورتمك (örtmek), from Proto-Turkic *ört- (“to cover”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ört-, “to cover”), Azerbaijani örtmək (“to cover, shut”), Chuvash витме (vitme, “to cover, protect,

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اورتیلو (örtülü) or اورتیلی (örtüli, “covered, veiled; roofed; shut, closed”), from اورتی (örtü), from Proto-Turkic *ört- (“to cover”), from *ör- (“to plait”), morphologically ört- + -ü (deverbal nominal suffix) + -lü.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوری (örü), from Old Anatolian Turkish اورو (örü), from Proto-Turkic *ȫrü, ultimately a derivation from Proto-Turkic *ȫr- (“to rise”).

From Ottoman Turkish اورمجك (örümcek), اورومجك (örümcek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫrmekči (“spider”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (örümçek), Azerbaijani hörümçək, Bashkir үрмәксе (ürmäkse), Gagauz örümcä, Tatar үрмәкүч (ürmäküç), Uyghur ئۆمۈچۈك (ömüchük), Uzbek oʻrgimchak (“spider”). Literall
From Proto-Turkic *ös- (“to grow”).

parole.significato: (of a bird) to sing; (of a cock) to crow
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوتمك (ötmek, “to resound, ring, echo, to sing; crow”), from Proto-Turkic *öt- (“to sing (of birds), say, ask”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (öt-, “(of animals) to sing, make noise”), [script needed] (ötün-, “to ask, request”), Chagatai [script needed] (ötm

From Ottoman Turkish اوتوری (ötüri), equivalent to the obsolete verb öt- (“to pass”) + -eri (“towards”). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *öt- (“to pass by”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ötrü, “due to”) and Azerbaijani ötrü

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوگمك (öğmek, “to praise”), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوكمك (ögmek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫg- (“to praise”). cognates Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰇𐰏 (ög-, “to praise”), Karakhanid اۥوکْماكْ (ȫgmēk, “to praise”), Turkmen öwmek (“to compliment, praise”), Azerbaijani öymək (“t
From Proto-Turkic *ödkün- (“to imitate”), cognate with Yakut үтүгүн (ütügün, “to imitate”).
From Ottoman Turkish اوز (öz, “pith, essence, marrow; self”), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوز (öz), from Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ.
From Ottoman Turkish اوز (öz, “valley, river”), from Proto-Turkic *örs, *örsen (“river, river bed”).

parole.significato: inner part of a thing, center
parole.testo: A derivation of Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ. Cognate with Kazakh өзек (özek), Azerbaijani özək, etc.

parole.significato: Attention and care given to a task at hand; pains.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوزن (üzen, özen, “pains, pains-taking”), from اوز (öz, “pith, essence, the self”), from Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ (“inside, the essential part, the self”), morphologically öz + -en.

From Proto-Turkic *ögüŕ (“small river”). Compare Karakhanid اُوزْ (öz, “small river between two mountains”), اُكُزْ (öküz, ögüz, ügüz, “river; ox”), Old Turkic 𐰇𐰏𐰕 (ẅg²z, “small river”). Cognates with Azerbaijani özən, Tatar үзән (üzän), Kazakh өзен (özen).

parole.significato: To aspire to be like somebody one admires; to emulate something or someone.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوزنمك (üzenmek, “to take pains, to be pains-taking”), from Ottoman Turkish اوز (öz, “pith, essence, the self”), from Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ (“inside, the essential part, the self”).

parole.significato: The effort to be or look like someone or something one likes.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوزنمك (üzenmek, “to take pains, to be pains-taking”), from Ottoman Turkish اوز (öz, “pith, essence, the self”), from Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ (“inside, the essential part, the self”), morphologically öz + -en + -ti.
From Ottoman Turkish اوزكه (özge), from Proto-Turkic *öŕge (“other”). Cognate with Kazakh өзге (özge).
From Ottoman Turkish اوج (öc), from Proto-Turkic *ȫč.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكرنمك (öğrenmek, “to learn”), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوكرنمك (ögrenmek, “to learn”), from Proto-Turkic *ögren-. See also öğretmek (“to teach”), causative form of the same root. Cognates Cognate with Karakhanid [script needed] (ögrenmēk, “to learn”), Azerbaijani ö
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكرتمك (öğretmek, “to teach”), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوكرتمك (ögretmek), from Proto-Turkic *ögret- (“to teach”).
From Ottoman Turkish اوگون (öğün), from Proto-Turkic *ödün, a development of *öd (“time”) and thus related to اویله (öyle, “noon”).
From Ottoman Turkish اوكورمك (öğürmek), from Proto-Turkic *ȫkür- (“to belch, nauseate”).

parole.significato: to grind something into powder, to pulverize
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوگوتمك (öğütmek), from Proto-Turkic *ǖk- (“to grind, crush”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ükit-).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكش (üğüş, üküş), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوكش (/⁠üküş, ügüş⁠/), from Proto-Turkic *üküĺ (“many”).
From Proto-Turkic *ür-.
From Ottoman Turkish اولشمك (üleşmek), from Proto-Turkic *üle-.

From Ottoman Turkish اولكه, اولكا (ülke), from Proto-Turkic *üle- (“to divide”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ülkä, “administrative region”); Kazakh өлке (ölke), Kyrgyz өлкө (ölkö, “country, land”), Kumyk уьлке (ülke, “country”), Uzbek oʻlka (“region, country”), Uyghur ئۆلكە (ölke, “coun
From Ottoman Turkish اوك (üñ), from Proto-Turkic *ǖn. Compare Old Turkic [script needed] (ün).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اورهمك (üremek), from Old Anatolian Turkish اورمك (üremek), from Proto-Turkic *üdre- (“to reproduce”). Cognate with Azerbaijani ürəmək.

parole.significato: to fear, be afraid of, dread, wince
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوركمك (ürkmek), from Proto-Turkic *ürk- (“to be afraid”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ürk-, “to be afraid, run away in fear”), Kyrgyz үркүү (ürküü, “to be frightened of”), Southern Altai ӱркӱӱр (ürküür), Uzbek hurkmoq, Kazakh үрку (ürküw, “to be frightened of”), Ba

parole.significato: The feeling of being afraid or frightened; fright.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوركنتی (ürküntü, “a sudden fright, panic”), from Ottoman Turkish اوركمك (ürkmek, “to be frightened, to start with fright, especially for a horse to shy”), from Proto-Turkic *ürk- (“to be afraid”), morphologically ürk- + -ün + -tü.

parole.significato: To tremble, to shudder, to have goose bumps due to fear, loathing or cold.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اورپرمك (ürpermek, “for one's hair to stand on end”), from Proto-Turkic *ürper- (“for one's hair to stand on end”), from Proto-Turkic *ürüp (“raised, fluffy”) with the suffix -ar.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اورومك (ürümek), from Old Anatolian Turkish اورمك (ürmek, üremek), from Proto-Turkic *ür- (“to blow”). According to Nişanyan, final "ü" in ürü- in Turkish is a later development and not well understood. The original ür- and the earlier variant üre- can still be found i
From Proto-Turkic *ürüŋ (“white”). Cognate with Old Uyghur [script needed] (ürüŋ, “white”), Karakhanid [script needed] (ürüŋ, “white”), Yakut үрүҥ (ürüŋ, “white”), Old Turkic 𐰇𐰼𐰭 (ürüŋ, “white”).

parole.significato: something's face or side looking upwards or towards the sky
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوست (üst), from Proto-Turkic *üŕ-t (“on top, high above”), derivative of *ǖŕ. Cognate with üzeri.

parole.significato: To singe to remove hair on a person or on an animal's skin/hide.
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *üt-.

parole.significato: To beat in a game, to defeat.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اوتمق (utmak) or اوتمك (ütmek, ötmek), from Old Anatolian Turkish اوتمق (utmaq), from Proto-Turkic *ut-. Cognates Azerbaijani udmaq Karakhanid اُتْماقْ (utmaq) Old Turkic 𐰆𐱃- (wt¹-) Turkmen utmak Uyghur ئۇتماق (utmaq) Uzbek yutmoq

parole.significato: step- (Used in the words starting in English with the syllable step-, such as üvey kız (stepdaughter).)
parole.testo: From Proto-Turkic *ögey. Cognate to Azerbaijani ögey.

parole.significato: turtle dove, any of several birds in the genus Streptopelia, especially Streptopelia turtur
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكیك (üğeyik, üveyik, “turtle dove”), from Proto-Turkic *ögey- (“to coo”). Cognate with Salar üngülük.

parole.significato: some small kind of fly, similar to a mosquito or gnat
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ایوز (ivez, “gadfly”), from Proto-Turkic *uyaz (“some kind of gnat or mosquito”).
From Ottoman Turkish اوزنگی (üzengi), from Proto-Turkic *üŕeŋgü (“stirrup”), from *yüŕeŋgü, from *yüŕ (“ring”). Cognate to Bashkir өҙәңге (öðäñge), see there for more cognates.
